item.title: 'The threat is finally real': Judge rips White House 'weaponization'
item.description: A D.C. magistrate judge has issued a scathing written order ripping the Trump administration for what he described as the blatant "weaponization" of law enforcement.

item.title: Army detonates toxic bomb-making materials at Iowa plant following delays
item.description: The Army detonated nearly five tons of lead azide at an ammunition plant in Iowa.

item.title: LIVE: Lead azide detonation at Iowa Army base: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Trump announces new tariffs on EU, China despite US midterms defeat
item.description: President Donald Trump's administration on Wednesday reignited global trade tensions by proposing new tariffs on some of the largest US trading partners, including the EU, Japan and Taiwan. China could be slapped with a 20 percent tariff, a senior official said. The announcement came weeks after a cost-of-living crisis landed the Republicans a sweeping defeat in the US midterms.

item.title: US plans to hike tariffs on China, EU, Brazil and others over subsidized production
item.description: President Donald Trump's administration is getting ready to raise tariffs on China, the European Union and a dozen other trading partners

item.title: How American Thanksgiving took root -- and evolved -- in Liberia
item.description: The first settlers of Liberia were African Americans who brought along the holiday of Thanksgiving — which has evolved to reflect the history and identity of this new nation. (Image credit: Eddie Raynes)

item.title: California braces for flooding threat from huge tides, El Nino
item.description: Californians are preparing for a confluence of exceptionally high tides and El Nino-fueled weather that threatens coastal areas with extreme flooding during the busiest US travel week of the year. The San Francisco Bay Area is expected to get hit hard with a one-two punch of inclement weather and monster tides, which forecasters warned could push seawater into low-lying areas on Wednesday and Thursday.

item.title: 'Historic' space mission: China launches Shenzhou 24 spacecraft carrying Pakistani astronaut
item.description: China on Wednesday launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts — two Chinese and a Pakistani — sending the first foreign crew member to its space station. It successfully separated from a rocket and entered its predetermined orbit. The launch marked the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China’s crewed space program.

item.title: WATCH: 'Dancing with the Stars' superfan gets special surprise
item.description: A lucky superfan receives two tickets to the "Dancing with the Stars" live show on Feb. 16, including a behind-the-scenes tour, a meet-and-greet and exclusive merchandise.

item.title: 'Utterly broken' mother pays tribute to son found fatally injured in hospital car park
item.description: An "utterly broken" mother has paid tribute to her son, who died after being found seriously injured in a hospital car park in a suspected murder.

item.title: Colombian authorities rescue all hostages held at Cartagena supermarket
item.description: Security forces rescued all the hostages held for nearly a day at a supermarket in the northern Colombian tourist city of Cartagena, President Abelardo de la Espriella said early Wednesday. The president said that the men were “common criminals” who fled into the supermarket after a failed attempt to hold up an armored truck. The hostage situation broke out as Colombia is experiencing a wave of attacks by rebel groups on government targets.

item.title: Violence against women in the digital age: When the internet becomes a weapon
item.description: November 25th is the United Nation's International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. In the age of social media and artificial intelligence, there are now new spaces in which violence against women has appeared, with the internet now a growing weapon in the hands of abusers. 85% of women who spend time online have witnessed violence, and 38% have been the target of it.

item.title: What to know before using AI agents for Black Friday shopping
item.description: 59% of U.S. shoppers plan to use AI for holiday shopping this weekend, according to the National Retail Federation (Image credit: Heather Diehl)

item.title: US army to detonate stockpile of unstable bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
item.description: The US military will on Wednesday detonate some 10,000 pounds of unstable and degraded explosive material in Iowa, where local residents were urged to evacuate amid concerns over possible toxic lead contamination. US officials say the 68 drums of lead azide are at risk of spontaneous explosion. A series of safety measures are being taken to curb potential contamination from the blast, but the Army has encouraged residents of a small town and other nearby areas to leave "out of an abundance of caution."

item.title: The forgotten victims of femicide: Children orphaned by violence in Italy
item.description: November 25th is International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. The forgotten victims of femicide are the children who find themselves motherless, often because their mother was killed by their own father. Italy recorded 97 female homicides in 2025 – 62 of them were committed by a partner. These crimes leave whole families devastated and children who have to grow up without their parents. FRANCE 24’s correspondent in Italy, Natalia Mendoza, reports.

item.title: WATCH: Thanksgiving travel rush underway
item.description: Major airlines already offering travel waivers in the wake of the Thanksgiving travel rush as a collision between a plane and catering truck at JFK airport creates delays.

item.title: Powerful storm threatens East Coast with hurricane-level flooding, damaging winds
item.description: More than 31 million people are under coastal flood warnings along both coasts as a powerful storm takes shape, bringing the threat of hurricane-level flooding.

item.title: Israeli MPs advance bill for inquiry into security failings that led to October 7 Hamas attack
item.description: Israeli MPs on Wednesday gave their initial approval for the creation of a commission to investigate the security failures that led to the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas. Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who was in power when the attack happened, has repeatedly rejected calls to set up such a probe.

item.title: Producer and guitarist Ginton on jazz, remixing big hits and collaborating on a track for Drake
item.description: Amsterdam-based guitarist, DJ and music producer Ginton is known for blending reggae, Afro, Caribbean and electronic music. He told FRANCE 24 that his background in jazz was "the reason I can make the music I make today". He also told us of his "surprise" in collaborating on a track for Drake's album "Honestly, Nevermind". He spoke to us in Perspective.

item.title: WATCH: Best and worst times to drive
item.description: ABC News' Rhiannon Ally provides the latest updates on the road as gas prices drop, offering some relief for drivers this Thanksgiving.

item.title: WATCH: Australian man bikes 10,000 miles across 48 US states
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to ultra cyclist Jack Thompson, who rode through all 48 states in the contiguous U.S., covering almost 10,000 miles in 60 days.

item.title: WATCH: Tourist killed in wild elephant attack while hiking with tour group
item.description: A Swiss man was killed when elephants charged at a tour group in Mount Cameroon National Park, Cameroon authorities confirmed to ABC News.

item.title: Serial rapist who preyed on women in UK and abroad jailed for 17 years
item.description: A serial rapist who preyed on women in the UK and while abroad has been jailed for 17 years.

item.title: ‘A symbol of hope’: Pakistan celebrates as astronaut enters orbit
item.description: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali has become the first Pakistani to reach orbit after blasting off on board a Chinese mission to the country’s Tiangong space station on Tuesday. The Pakistan Air Force pilot and payload specialist’s feat was celebrated by cheers and rapturous applause by those watching in his homeland.

item.title: Violence against women: Its many forms and the paths to justice
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Wednesday, November 25: Some 21 percent of women say they have suffered "economic violence", while others are exploring new types of justice for their abusers. In other news, recent leaks on Russian troop losses show 349 deaths in Mali, Russia's biggest military deployment in Africa. As Spain prepares to head to the polls, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announces a raft of social measures. Finally, a plucky young cat from Essex has taken a train to London.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis claim attacks on Riyadh financial district, Saudi refinery
item.description: Yemen's Houthis on Wednesday claimed attacks targeting the financial district in the Saudi capital and the sprawling Ras Tanura refinery in the kingdom's oil-rich east, in retaliation for strikes on their territory. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree described the attack targeting the refinery as "accurate and direct", saying it "caused fires to break out at the facility". He said the attack on Riyadh was "carried out in three phases, with strikes hitting their targets accurately".

item.title: Greetings from Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest point in all its splendor
item.description: Climbing tall mountains like Kilimanjaro is a study in contrasts — from beating sun to freezing nights, fire and snow.

item.title: Cyberattack exposes unclassified information from CIA system, US media reports
item.description: A recently discovered hack on a CIA analysis system exposed some unclassified information, US media reported on Tuesday. The breach is the latest in a series of cyber attacks that have targeted US government departments and major companies in recent weeks.

item.title: RAF 'moving aircraft to hangars at night to protect them from drone threats'
item.description: The Royal Air Force is moving aircraft to hangars and hardened shelters at night to protect them from possible drone threats, it is understood.

item.title: Surprise Eurostar strike cancels London, Paris and Brussels trains
item.description: Several Eurostar trains connecting London, Paris and Brussels were cancelled in a surprise strike on Wednesday. The train operator did not specify who exactly was striking or the reasons why.

item.title: Buying new things feels wonderful. But it can also be a trap
item.description: Saying No to New , says that "you do feel joy and excitement" from buying new things initially — "but science says those feelings can't last."'/> Constantly buying new things can be problematic, says journalist Eric Athas, author of the new book "Saying No to New." Here's how to break the cycle and find joy in what you already have. (Image credit: ㅤ)

item.title: A quintessential Route 66 diner has been serving up Americana for nearly 100 years
item.description: The Ariston Cafe opened its doors in 1924 to serve travelers along Route 66 and has dished up classic American road fare ever since. (Image credit: Neeta Satam for NPR)

item.title: In a time of rising costs, one Thanksgiving commodity is cheaper: cannabis
item.description: Steep discounts for "Green Wednesday," one of the highest-selling days for cannabis, help customers keep costs down. But experts say retailers are feeling the pinch. (Image credit: Haven Daley/AP)

item.title: Eurostar trains cancelled and delayed over 'unannounced strike action'
item.description: Several Eurostar trains have been cancelled or delayed due to "unannounced strike action", the company said.

item.title: China investigates Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
item.description: The Politburo member is the latest senior official targeted in President Xi Jinping's long-running anti-corruption campaign, which has shown no signs of letting up in scope or depth. (Image credit: Ng Han Guan)

item.title: Two men appear in court accused of stealing cufflinks and a clock from William and Kate's home
item.description: Two men have appeared in court accused of stealing cufflinks and a clock from the Norfolk home of the Prince and Princess of Wales.

item.title: Army plans to detonate nearly five tons of lead-based explosives in Iowa
item.description: The controlled explosion is scheduled to take place at 9 a.m. CT/10 a.m ET at the Iowa Ammunition Plant, according to U.S. Army officials. (Image credit: Austin Johnson)

item.title: Time runs out for Poundland as directors prepare for administration
item.description: The directors of Poundland are preparing to appoint administrators as soon as Wednesday afternoon, raising fears for thousands of jobs in what would be the British high street's biggest collapse for a decade.

item.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia leaves U.S. voluntarily for Spain
item.description: Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran immigrant who became a symbol of Trump's mass deportation campaign, voluntarily left the country on Tuesday after nearly two years of legal battles. (Image credit: Alex Wong)

item.title: Pentagon hires conservative contractors to audit military base schools
item.description: The Defense Department continues to revamp its schools for military families to align with conservative education ideals

item.title: Multiple chances missed to protect two-year-old murdered by his grandparents, report finds
item.description: Agencies missed numerous opportunities to protect a two-year-old who was murdered by his grandparents, a report has found.

item.title: Two children among six dead in plane crash
item.description: Divers have found the bodies of six people, including two children, after a plane crashed off the coast of Mississippi on Tuesday, according to the US Coast Guard.

item.title: AFCON 2025: CAS gives title back to Senegal as Morocco vows to challenge verdict
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has handed down its ruling: Senegal is officially the 2025 AFCON champion. The Moroccan Football Federation has announced that it will challenge the verdict, citing irregularities in the proceedings.

item.title: Amnesty calls for ICC genocide probe over Israel's impact on births in Gaza
item.description: Amnesty International on Wednesday urged the International Criminal Court to investigate whether Israeli officials committed genocide in Gaza, citing measures it says have prevented births and severely harmed women's reproductive health. The rights group said it had serious concerns that these effects were intentional, while acknowledging it could not reach a definitive conclusion.

item.title: Live: Two Libyan soldiers killed in Ukrainian attack on Russian vessels in Benghazi
item.description: Two Libyan soldiers have died from injuries sustained in an attack, claimed by Ukraine, on Russian ships near Benghazi, a senior figure in the administration in eastern Libya said late on Tuesday. Members of the European Parliament will convene in Strasbourg on Wednesday to discuss "Europe’s role and capacity to protect the international order and secure a just and lasting peace for Ukraine". Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

item.title: Ukraine seeks €115 billion in foreign aid for 2027, Zelensky says
item.description: Ukraine will need €115 billion in external financing next year to sustain its economy and war effort against Russia, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, adding that Kyiv had secured commitments for about €90 billion from the European Union.

item.title: New York jury convicts Huawei of stealing trade secrets
item.description: A New York jury on Tuesday found Chinese telecom giant Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets and other criminal offences, but acquitted it of a racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. The verdict followed a three-month trial in New York in a case that adds to longstanding US efforts to curb Huawei's operations over alleged threats to national security.

item.title: Champions League: Real Madrid thrash PSV in comeback win as Manchester City held by Napoli
item.description: Real Madrid extended their winning run to 10 games in all competitions on Tuesday, overturning an early deficit to rout PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League, with Jude Bellingham scoring a spectacular goal and Kylian Mbappé netting twice. Manchester City, meanwhile, twice came from behind to draw 2-2 with Napoli, while Arsenal were held to a 1-1 draw by Borussia Dortmund.

item.title: WATCH: President Trump holds Thanksgiving turkey pardoning ceremony
item.description: President Donald Trump held the annual Thanksgiving turkey pardon ceremony at the White House on Tuesday.

item.title: Tech executives' investment in Trump 'clearly paying off' as Huang reinstated at Nvidia
item.description: Nvidia shares fell on Tuesday as the historic rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return as CEO quickly lost steam, with investors refocusing ​on the political ‌and governance risks surrounding his reinstatement. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, The Hill Senior Technology Reporter Miranda Nazzaro says that the reinstatement of Huang at Nvidia represents "the culmination of a two-year push of tech executives to get closer to President Trump and their investment in the president is clearly paying off".

item.title: WATCH: Viral 'DWTS' fans talk season 35 finale
item.description: Superfans Giorgina Martino and Alex Foley and their baby London join ABC News Live to discuss the finale and what they think are some of the most shocking moments from the season.

item.description: Trump pardoned Giuliani last year.

item.title: Colombian police storm supermarket, freeing hostages and killing gunman
item.description: Colombian police have stormed a supermarket and freed at least 20 people who were being held hostage, killing one of the gunmen.

item.description: Blanche described Nvidia as "a good corporate citizen."

item.title: Huawei guilty of plotting to steal trade secrets and bank fraud
item.description: Chinese tech giant Huawei, has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud after a landmark trial in the US.

item.title: They want to watch Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan die but the Army won’t let them
item.description: Julia Wilson was nine months pregnant when she found herself caught in gunfire at Fort Hood in 2009. 'It's crazy how quickly things run through your brain," she said.

item.title: Groups push back on Trump administration changes to historical monument
item.description: Two Philadelphia groups filed a federal lawsuit against the Trump administration over the removal of panels at the slavery memorial at the President’s House site.

item.description: Thomas Markle has been formally charged on two counts of possessing child sexual abuse material in Los Angeles.

item.description: ABC News' Rhiannon Ally highlights how the Dallas Cowboys are celebrating three decades of giving back to their community during Thanksgiving.

item.title: WATCH: Detroit Lions help feed their community this Thanksgiving
item.description: ABC News' Will Reeve shares how the Detroit Lions are carrying on a Thanksgiving tradition of giving back to those in need.

item.title: Trump granted new chance to potentially erase his hush money case
item.description: An appeals court is giving President Trump a new chance to move his criminal hush money case into federal court, where he could then attempt to overturn his conviction.

item.title: Trump owned at least $12 million in Nvidia stock at the end of last year
item.description: President Donald Trump owned at least $12 million in Nvidia stock at the end of 2025, according to his annual financial disclosure report reviewed by ABC News.

item.title: WATCH: 'Dancing with the Stars' watch parties on tap for live season finale
item.description: Millions of "Dancing with the Stars" fans are already warming up their popcorn poppers and fondue pots -- with others turning the show's finale into an epic night out.

item.title: China 'sentences official to death for spying'
item.description: China has sentenced to death an official who was said to have leaked state secrets to a foreign country.

item.title: FA chair had to sign NDA to view FIFA documents on World Cup sell-off
item.description: Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt has now viewed some FIFA documents on the World Cup sell-off but had to sign a nondisclosure agreement, Sky News has learned.

item.title: WATCH: Preparing for annual White House turkey pardon
item.description: Two turkeys named Freedom and Feather are set to get Thanksgiving pardons from President Donald Trump Tuesday.

item.title: WATCH: As the holiday season nears, experts warn against so-called porch pirates
item.description: Millions of packages are stolen each year, but AI tools and porch cameras can help prevent theft.

item.title: Morocco 'astonished' at decision to restore Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations champions
item.description: Senegal have been awarded the Africa Cup of Nations title after successfully appealing against the decision to strip them of it.

item.title: Gisele Pelicot 'deeply shocked' as nude photos of her sent to media
item.description: Gisele Pelicot has said she is "deeply shocked" and "humiliated" after nude images of her were sent to the media without her consent to promote a new book about coercive control.

item.title: Navy keeps Black war hero's name on carrier after weighing renaming it for Trump
item.description: Navy officials had weighed renaming the vessel for Trump, sources said.

item.title: Deadly fire at confectionery factory kills 24 as rescuers search for dozens still missing
item.description: A deadly fire that tore through a confectionery factory in Indonesia has claimed the lives of 24 people, with 34 others still missing.

item.title: Murder investigation launched as woman 80, dies after being set on fire
item.description: Police have launched a murder investigation after an 80-year-old woman who was set on fire outside her flat died.
